newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
--A three percent increase to public servants - based on the difference between current and forecast 1997 inflation - is the only clear wage increase the government is prepared to give.

--The government may yet be forced to turn to the solution of new taxes to ensure revenues for next year's budget, despite efforts to keep election pledge of 'no new taxes'. New taxes will most probably take the form of taxation of state bonds and T-bills and of large real estate holdings.
--Capital Market Commission examining a framework which would allow the lending and sale of share titles.

--Government's plans to make Greece a regional energy centre centre on construction of two new production plants - one to export electrical power to Bulgaria and the other to Albania, Italy and the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.

--Bourse inquiry into insider trading shows no violations. --Tax exemptions: who they favour and who they hurt. Panteios University study shows who stands to gain the most from the abolition of tax exemptions.

--Finance ministry report shows self-employed professionals, merchants, industry and high-income earners best use prevailing tax breaks and have been targeted by the government as those "haves" who must bear the brunt of convergence.

--Pensioners and wage-earners will again bear the largest tax burden next year. The readjustment of wealth indicators (which largely affects low and middle income earners), the lack of a pegged cost of living index, nominal increases in wages and pensions will lead to additional tax burdens.
--Twenty-two products and services the 'hard core of inflation' bedevilling the consumer price index in January-September 1996 period, development ministry says.

--Olympic Airways plans cooperation and alliances with airline companies from around the world, in an effort to contain operating costs, increase passenger traffic and destinations and better services.
--Greek firms bid to play the leading role in investment and exports to the Balkans, despite massive problems in each country and a lag in realising the advantages.

--Greek National Tourism Organisation (EOT) Secretary-General Vassilis Kourtesis says offers for international advertising campaign will end November. Policies aims at tourist infrastructure through works.
